title: G01 pre-production workflow scope reset
description: Establish one registry-driven YouTube Pre-production / Director Factory workflow and detach legacy production capabilities from the default project journey without deleting compatibility code.
businessContext: New Topic, Existing Script, and Reference projects need a truthful pre-production journey through GG Lab image review and production handoff; existing SQLite projects must remain loadable.
acceptanceCriteria: A single registry defines ordered pre-production stages, applicability, dependencies, interaction requirements, artifact contracts, routes, and invalidation relationships without a hardcoded total.
Topic, Existing Script, and Reference project modes resolve truthful applicable and not_applicable stages; skipped stages are never fake-approved and do not enter the required-progress denominator.
New projects can reach Production Handoff without image/video-model certification, TTS, FFmpeg, CapCut, stock, or image-provider requirements.
Project creation, persistence loading, and runtime normalization safely support new workflow data and legacy projects with unknown or missing stage data.
Opening a project resolves its current applicable stage from workflow metadata/state and new projects are never routed to TTS, FFmpeg, CapCut, preview, QA, or export routes.
The creator project journey visibly renders dynamic stage state and overall progress, including optional and not_applicable states where useful.
Focused domain, persistence, routing, renderer, and Electron/runtime tests cover all three new modes plus a legacy fixture and restart behavior.
Independent reviewer and QA evidence are recorded before integration.
humanEscalationConditions: A compatibility change would overwrite existing project data or user files.
Implementation must change an excluded provider, rendering, queue, or CapCut package.
The latest-main baseline fails in an unrelated area after targeted isolation.
An unresolved product-mode distinction changes the documented G01 workflow contract.
